changes.headline: EIA prints an 8.6 Mbbl draw; WTI leads the week, Brent stalls
changes.dek: EIA week ending Oct 9 (released Oct 15, delayed): crude excl. SPR 415.6 Mbbl (-8.6), distillate 102.6 (-2.5), Cushing +1.86 to about 26.6 (five-month high), utilization 93.5%, production 13,679 kb/d (-300, Isaias week). WTI Nov26 settled Thu $97.97 (+$2.88, +3.03%), Brent Dec26 $105.92 (-$0.14); overnight WTI $97.20 (-$0.77) / Brent $105.21 (-$0.71); week: WTI +5.81%, Brent +0.44%. The delayed EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending Oct 9 printed a crude draw of 8.6 Mbbl to 415.6 Mbbl against a consensus expectation near flat, the steepest draw in over two months. Gasoline built 3.5 Mbbl to 208.3, distillate drew 2.5 to 102.6 Mbbl (11.7 percent below the five-year seasonal average), Cushing built 1.86 Mbbl to about 26.6 Mbbl (a five-month high), utilization rose to 93.5 percent, and production fell 300 kb/d to 13,679 kb/d on the Hurricane Isaias shut-in week. The SPR was flat at 283 Mbbl. Thursday settles split: WTI Nov26 $97.97 (+3.03 percent), Brent Dec26 $105.92 (-$0.14); overnight Friday WTI $97.20 and Brent $105.21. The week's 5.81 percent WTI gain against Brent's 0.44 percent says the marginal bid was a US inventory story on a Hormuz premium that held without extending.
changes.balance_read: The production and Gulf lines are storm accounting that reverses next week; the durable lines are the distillate draw at low seasonal levels and a national draw that beat consensus by about 8.7 Mbbl. Cushing building to a five-month high inside a draw week is a delivery-point detail, not a balance signal.
changes.publishers: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, released Oct 15, 2026; Reuters, Oct 16, 2026, 0352 GMT snapshot and Thursday settles

changes.headline: Hormuz clearance at 68 percent of baseline; crack prints below $100 as the IEA accelerates releases
changes.dek: Kpler: total Hormuz clearance averaged 11.62 Mb/d over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.15 Mb/d baseline, slower and uneven recovery expected. Diesel crack $97.30 on the latest validated overnight bar, below $100 after nine straight days above (37 total days); 3-2-1 $54.25. IEA board (Oct 15): accelerate the remaining ~100 Mbbl of the March release (about 330 Mbbl released, total to exceed 400 Mbbl), including 20+ Mbbl of diesel as soon as possible; no new releases announced. Kpler data reported Thursday put total Hormuz clearance at an average of 11.62 Mb/d over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68 percent of the 17.15 Mb/d baseline, with intensified Iranian attacks driving Gulf crude flows sharply lower and a slower, more uneven recovery expected without a comprehensive political deal. Iran says it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions. No new vessel attack was confirmed overnight. The diesel crack printed $97.30 on the latest validated overnight bar, its first print below $100 after nine consecutive days above, with the 3-2-1 at $54.25 (maxima: diesel $117.92 Sep 16, 3-2-1 $75.31 Aug 28). The IEA governing board on Thursday agreed to accelerate completion of the remaining roughly 100 Mbbl of the March emergency release, including more than 20 Mbbl of diesel as soon as possible; the total will exceed the original 400 Mbbl, no new releases were announced, and members held over 200 Mbbl of diesel in public stocks as of Oct 7.
changes.balance_read: The flow impairment is now measured, not inferred, and Brent's 0.44 percent weekly gain says it is being carried rather than compounded. The crack's break came the morning after governments aimed diesel supply at it, but 20 Mbbl is under a day of global diesel use and the release is a completion schedule, not a new tranche: the break confirms on physical arrivals and stock builds, not on one overnight bar.
changes.publishers: Kpler via Reuters, Oct 15, 2026; validated crack history, refreshed Oct 16, 2026; IEA governing board statement via Reuters, Oct 15, 2026

changes.headline: Ukraine's resumption executed at Ryazan; WCS December widens to -$26.75 on 805 lots
changes.dek: Ukrainian drone attack sparked a fire at a Ryazan-region refinery on Thursday (regional governor, via Reuters); no Russian diesel loading. WCS Dec26 -$26.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 15), down $0.50 on 805 lots; C5 Dec26 +$4.00, down $1.25 on 100 lots; SYN Nov26 +$7.55 into today's Syncrude coker wrap; ARV-TMW December +$8.85. Houthis struck the Aden presidential palace complex Thursday (two guards killed); Riyadh airport reopening scheduled Oct 17. Ukraine's declared resumption of refinery strikes was executed on Thursday: a major drone attack on Russia's Ryazan region sparked a fire at an oil refinery, the regional governor said; damage is being assessed and no capacity figure has been published. No Russian diesel cargo has loaded. Canadian diffs (ICE, Oct 15): TMW Dec26 -$26.75, down $0.50 on 805 lots, the widest print of the episode; Nov26 -$24.96 on zero volume. ARV Dec26 -$17.90; ARV-TMW December +$8.85. SYN Nov26 +$7.55 (+$0.10) ahead of the Syncrude coker return wrapping Oct 16. C5 Dec26 +$4.00, down $1.25 on 100 lots, as the fall maintenance season ends. MSW Nov26 -$0.50; UHC Dec26 +$3.00. In Yemen, Houthi missiles struck the presidential palace complex in Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, and the Saudi-led coalition detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure; Aramco operations had continued normally and the supply count remains zero. AESO Oct 16, 01:39 MDT: all monitored SAGD cogen units at full maximum capability, grid Normal.
changes.balance_read: December heavy is pricing the seasonal wide ahead of the November apportionment notice (about Oct 19), on traded volume rather than formula marks. SYN holding its premium into the return, against a $1.25 C5 markdown, says the light side is not yet pricing returning SCO; the week after a clean Syncrude return is the test, with +$7.00 the pre-registered line.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 15-16, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 15, 2026; AESO CSD, Oct 16, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz flows at 68 percent of baseline; premium carried, not compounding
flags.detail: Kpler puts total Hormuz clearance at 11.62 Mb/d over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68 percent of the 17.15 Mb/d baseline, with a slower and uneven recovery expected. Brent gained 0.44 percent on the week the impairment covers. The risk is clearance falling further or a strike hitting Saudi process, pipeline or export assets. Trigger: Hormuz clearance falls materially below the 11.62 Mb/d seven-day average, or a strike hits Saudi process, pipeline or export assets

flags.title: Crack below $100 on the overnight print; IEA diesel acceleration is the test
flags.detail: The diesel crack printed $97.30 after nine straight days above $100, the morning after the IEA board accelerated the remaining ~100 Mbbl of releases with 20+ Mbbl of diesel front-loaded. No new release tranche was announced and US distillate stocks drew to 11.7 percent below the seasonal average. The break confirms on arrivals and stock builds. Trigger: IEA diesel arrivals publish timing and land, or a US distillate stock build prints

flags.title: SPR 40 Mbbl award still pending, ten days after bids
flags.detail: No DOE press announcement on the sixth solicitation as of early Friday, ten days after the Oct 6 bid deadline, and the DOE newsroom still shows the Sep 29 solicitation as its latest item. DOE's posted contracts tell the program story without one: 133.56 Mbbl already lent to 13 companies across the spring rounds, Trafigura the largest borrower at about 34 Mbbl (25.7 percent), ahead of Marathon (12.4 Mbbl) and ExxonMobil (11.4 Mbbl); trading houses took 45 percent of the total against 38 percent for refiners (posted contracts tallied Oct 13). The pending award adds 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery when it lands. Trigger: DOE announces the exchange award

forward_calendar.what: CFTC COT release (positioning as of Oct 13)
forward_calendar.detail: First read on how the book traded the escalation week: the Hormuz sinkings, Wednesday's three-week WTI high and Thursday's fade fall inside the window. Last vintage (as-of Oct 6): WTI managed-money net +53,598, 29th percentile; Brent net +201,052.

SCO supply returns into late October, softening SYN against WCS. SYN Nov26 settled at +$7.55 on Oct 15, ahead of the return; the pre-registered line is +$7.00 a week after a clean return. Suncor Edmonton/Base Plant fall work ended Oct 13 and the Horizon upgrader turnaround implies completion about Oct 12 to 13.

forward_calendar.what: Riyadh King Khalid airport closure scheduled to end
forward_calendar.detail: The airport has been closed to 21:00 GMT Oct 17 after the Houthi strikes. Whether it reopens on schedule is a read on Saudi air-defence confidence after the Dhahran Aramco HQ strike and renewed Houthi threats against airports and oil facilities.
Decides whether the binding-from-November base case is right; December TMW is already pricing the seasonal wide (-$26.75, ICE settle Oct 15, on 805 lots).

Bids went in Oct 6 (11:00 a.m. CT); a clean award prices 40 Mbbl of medium sour into the Gulf for Nov-Dec delivery. No award announced ten days later; DOE posted contracts already show 133.56 Mbbl lent to 13 companies in the spring rounds, Trafigura largest at about 34 Mbbl.
Next scheduled OPEC+ meeting; quotas are not the constraint, actual supply is.
